note: St Helena, read in the Revised Edition of the Laws on sainthelena.gov.sh (2026-10-31); Ascension and Tristan da Cunha have their own laws, which apply St Helena's only by their own orders, and weren't read, so this file is St Helena's. Majority: no St Helena ordinance sets it; the English Law (Application) Ordinance, 2005 (Ordinance 10 of 2005, in force 1 January 2006, consolidated to Ordinance 9 of 2025), s. 3, applies the Acts of Parliament in force in England on 1 January 2006 so far as suitable to local circumstances, which include the Family Law Reform Act 1969, s. 1: full age at eighteen (legislation.gov.uk). That the 1969 Act applies under s. 3 is my reading. Work: the Welfare of Children Ordinance, 2008 (Ordinance 14 of 2008, in force 1 March 2010, as amended to Ordinance 16 of 2017, revised edition 2017), s. 157B: no child under 18 may be employed except from 16 in work that isn't hazardous, light work from 13, and work experience from 11; none between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. unless supervised, and none in school hours for a child of compulsory school age (not held); s. 158 bars children under 15 from vessels other than family ones. Performers: the Ordinance makes no exception for performing, so a performer under 16 may only do light work from 13 and none younger (barred under 13; the 13-15 light-work route isn't held by the form). Service: none of the ordinances found sets military service, and St Helena has no defence force, so service is none (a reading from absence).
